key_insight: SynAgent transfers skills learned from single-agent human–object interactions into cooperative two-agent (human–object–human) behaviors, enabling scalable, physically plausible multi-agent humanoid manipulation with much less cooperative data.
problem_solved: Addresses severe data scarcity and coordination complexity in cooperative humanoid manipulation, improving generalization across diverse objects and multi-agent scenarios.
method: Learn rich single-agent human–object interaction skills from available solo demonstrations/simulations.
Apply a Solo-to-Cooperative synergy module that maps and adapts solo skills into coordinated multi-agent policies for two-agent manipulation.
Enforce physical plausibility and scalability through physics-aware constraints and simulation-driven policy refinement to handle diverse objects and contacts.
impact: Makes cooperative humanoid manipulation more data-efficient and generalizable, lowering the barrier for multi-agent embodied systems and accelerating deployment in robotics and virtual agents.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Solo skill learning → Solo-to-Cooperative synergy module → Coordinated two-agent execution
Before/After comparison: Solo-trained agents failing vs. SynAgent-enabled cooperative agents succeeding on the same object
Bar/line chart: Sample efficiency and generalization across object categories (solo vs. SynAgent)
Schematic of contact/force constraints showing physically plausible grasps and coordination roles
paper_title: SynAgent: Generalizable Cooperative Humanoid Manipulation via Solo-to-Cooperative Agent Synergy
paper_authors: Wei Yao, Haohan Ma, Hongwen Zhang, Yunlian Sun, Liangjun Xing
